explanation: The dips are short eclipses that repeat strictly every ~3.103 d, so this is an eclipsing binary. Each deep Gaia epoch (t=78.94, 376.77) is grey: G, BP and RP all drop by the same ~11%, both in fov 2, about 96 cycles apart. The 358.27 epoch falls about 0.11 d before a predicted minimum, consistent with catching ingress. An eclipse width of ~0.15-0.2 d fits t~2R/v for an A/F star in a 3.1-d orbit. A 17% depth implies a companion of ~0.4 R*, which is too large to be a planet. No secondary eclipse is seen, which points to a faint low-mass companion. The recurrence test puts all 50 events from Gaia and TESS into one pure phase window (aligned_fraction 1.0, purity 1.0, depth CV 0.15). TESS shows ~7% dips every ~1.21 d in two sectors years apart.
